# laravel-image-legacy

rv-life's unchanged fork of Folklore's `folklore/image`, a Composer package that resizes, crops and filters images inside a Laravel 5.1 to 5.7 app; which rv-life product uses it, if any, is Unknown.

## What it does

### Purpose
This is a library for Laravel apps that need to show the same uploaded image at different sizes and with simple effects. Instead of writing image code for each size, a developer builds an image URL with the size and effects written into the file name, and the package makes that version on request. It is Folklore's open-source package `folklore/image` (`composer.json`); rv-life holds a copy of it. Nothing in the repo says which rv-life product uses it or why it was forked.

### What it can do
- Make a changed version of an image from a specially formatted URL. For example, `/uploads/photo-image(300x300-crop-grayscale).jpg` returns `/uploads/photo.jpg` cut to 300 by 300 pixels in black and white (config `url_parameter` and `pattern` in `src/resources/config/image.php`).
- Build those URLs in PHP with `Image::url()`, or in the browser with the bundled `image.js` helper (`src/resources/assets/js/image.js`), which builds the same URL format.
- Change images in code with `Image::make()`, then save them, or work with the underlying Imagine library directly through `Image::open()`.
- Apply built-in changes: resize, crop (with a position), rotate, grayscale, negative (invert colours), gamma, blur, colorize and interlace (the `filter*` methods in `src/Folklore/Image/ImageManager.php`). Developers can register their own named filters with `Image::filter()`, and can limit URLs to those custom filters only (`serve_custom_filters_only`).
- Optionally save each changed image next to the original, so the web server can send the saved file directly on later requests without running PHP (`write_image`, off by default, and `write_path`).
- Optionally act as a proxy for images kept on another Laravel storage disk (by default the `cloud` disk) or at a remote URL: it fetches the original, changes it, can write the result back to that disk, and caches the response (`proxy*` settings, `src/Folklore/Image/ImageProxy.php`). The proxy is off by default.
- Delete an image together with every changed version of it, or only the changed versions (`delete()` and `deleteManipulated()`).

### How it works
When the package's service provider loads, it merges its config and, if `serve` is on (the default), adds a Laravel route that matches any image path containing the `-image(...)` part (`src/Folklore/Image/ImageServiceProvider.php`). A request to that route goes to `ImageController@serve`, which reads the size and options out of the file name, finds the original file in the source folders (by default the app's `public` folder, config `src_dirs`), applies the changes through the Imagine library with the GD, Imagick or Gmagick driver (config `driver`, default `gd`), and returns the image with long cache headers (31 days by default). A missing file or a bad option gives a 404; other errors give a 500. When `write_image` is on, the result is also saved to disk and an `ImageSaved` event fires. The proxy route works the same way but reads the original from a storage disk or over HTTP with Guzzle.

The package is complete and was in use as an open-source release: `master` is tag `v0.3.25`. This repository is a copy of the upstream project with no rv-life changes (see Status).

## Where it runs
- Deploy target: a package others install with Composer. `composer.json` names it `folklore/image`, and the previous README links its Packagist page. It does not run on its own; it runs inside whichever Laravel app installs it.
- Live URL or service name: none. The package adds routes to the host app; their URLs depend on that app.
- Environments: none defined in the repo.

| Runtime | Version the code pins | Version CI uses | Meets the floor |

| PHP | `>=5.5.9` (`composer.json`), with `illuminate/support` 5.1 to 5.7 | 5.5, 5.6, 7.0 and 7.1 (`.travis.yml`, Travis CI) | No. The floor is PHP 8.4 or newer; the pin allows versions far below it and CI tests none at or above it. |
| JavaScript (`src/resources/assets/js/image.js`) | no pin | not built or tested in CI | No floor applies: plain browser script, no Node runtime, no `package.json`. |

## How to run it locally
Unknown: no run instructions in the repo for running the package on its own. It is meant to be installed into a Laravel app. The steps below come from the previous README, corrected against the files:

1. Server needs: one of the PHP image extensions gd, Imagick or Gmagick, and the exif extension, which the package uses to work out an image's format.
2. Add it to the app's `composer.json`, for example `"folklore/image": "0.3.*"`, then run `composer install` or `composer update`.
3. On Laravel 5.5 and later the service provider `Folklore\Image\ImageServiceProvider` and the `Image` facade (`Folklore\Image\Facades\Image`) register themselves through `extra.laravel` in `composer.json`. On older versions add both to the app's `config/app.php`.
4. Publish the config and the browser script: `php artisan vendor:publish --provider="Folklore\Image\ImageServiceProvider"`. The config lands at `config/image.php` and the script under `public/vendor/folklore/image` (`ImageServiceProvider.php`).
5. Review `config/image.php`.

Environment variables: none. The package reads only Laravel config (`src/resources/config/image.php`), not the environment.

## How to test it
`vendor/bin/phpunit`, after `composer install` (`.travis.yml`, `phpunit.xml`). The suite uses Orchestra Testbench to boot a small Laravel app and runs three test files: `tests/ImageTestCase.php` (URL building), `tests/ImageServeTestCase.php` (serving: resize by width, height and crop, writing the image to disk and to a custom path, and 404s for a wrong option, a missing file and a wrong format) and `tests/ImageProxyTestCase.php` (the proxy route). Test images are in `tests/fixture/`. CI also installs the Imagick and Gmagick extensions (`scripts/install_php_extensions.sh`) and sends coverage to Coveralls on one job.

## How it is deployed
There is no deploy. `release.sh` is a manual release script: it fetches tags, commits any uncommitted changes, pushes `develop`, merges `develop` into `master`, tags the next version number and pushes `master` with tags to `origin`. How the tag reaches Packagist is not in the repo; Unknown. There are no GitHub Actions workflows (no `.github` folder). CI is Travis CI (`.travis.yml`), which tests but does not publish.

- Services it needs: the host app's filesystem; for the proxy, a Laravel storage disk (default `cloud`) or a remote HTTP source, and Laravel's cache. Travis CI and Coveralls for CI.

## Previous README: features, compatibility and roadmap
Kept from the previous README because it still matches the files or cannot be checked from them.

The package uses [Imagine](https://github.com/avalanche123/Imagine) for image manipulation. Imagine works with GD2, Imagick and Gmagick. It is inspired by [Croppa](https://github.com/BKWLD/croppa), which also uses formatted URLs.

From the previous README, not verified: the Laravel to package version table. Laravel 4.2 used package 0.1.x, Laravel 5.0 used 0.2.x, and Laravel 5.1 and 5.2 used 0.3.x. The current `composer.json` (0.3.x line) declares Laravel 5.1 to 5.7.

From the previous README, not verified: upstream documentation lives in the project wiki: [complete documentation](https://github.com/Folkloreatelier/image/wiki), [configuration options](https://github.com/Folkloreatelier/image/wiki/Configuration-options) and [image filters](https://github.com/Folkloreatelier/laravel-image/wiki/Image-filters).

From the previous README, not verified: upstream's roadmap listed more built-in filters such as brightness and contrast, more options when serving images, an Artisan command to manipulate images, and batch operations on many files. None of these is on `master`.

## Needs attention
- PHP below the floor: `composer.json` allows PHP `>=5.5.9`, and `.travis.yml` tests only PHP 5.5 to 7.1. The floor is PHP 8.4.
- The package declares Laravel 5.1 to 5.7 only (`composer.json`, `illuminate/support`), so a Laravel app on any newer version cannot install it.
- CI is Travis CI only (`.travis.yml`); there are no GitHub Actions workflows. The previous README's build badge pointed at upstream's Travis project, not this fork.
- The fork has no rv-life changes on any branch (git history), so it adds nothing over the upstream package; nothing in the repo shows that any rv-life app installs it from this fork.
- `release.sh` runs `git add .` and `git commit -am` before pushing, so it commits whatever is in the working copy.
- The old branches `feature/metadatareader`, `feature/proxy`, `v1`, `v1.1` and `v1.2` hold upstream's unreleased or later work (on `v1.2` the package is renamed `folklore/laravel-image`), which `upstream/master` does not have (git history).
